title: S03C phase 3/3: S03 CAPTURE lane: village life, the practice trainer, and the first night
_comment: CAPTURE lane for S03, seeded from the logic lane's run://S02-exit.json through the production title screen (seed_save -> boot -> Load -> await_load), which is the pattern §H.1 names.
_comment_generated: GENERATED by tools/gate_f/derive_capture_lane.py from S03.json. Do not hand-edit: change the source segment or the authored notes in the generator and regenerate, or the capture lane stops being the journey's own path and §H.1's provenance claim stops being true. `--check` fails CI-style if the two have drifted.
_comment_derivation: Kept: every step of S03 up to and including its last capture (index 507 of 572), minus note/defect/probe_cell/save_out and the four pacing asserts. 488 of 573 steps survive. Step ids carry their origin in `_derived_from`.
_comment_seeding: Run this into the SAME run directory as the logic lanes. Its `seed_save` steps resolve `run://` against that directory's saves, so a capture lane run anywhere else has no chapter to load and will stop at its first seed.
_comment_cost: Splits cleanly in two. The map tab and the street-level walk are genuine class B -- a load and a few tens of metres. The three night frames are the expensive end of the journey: 'first NATURAL nightfall' means the in-game hours S03 spends reaching it, and pin_clock is DIAG-only so a journey capture lane may not skip them. Any attempt to shorten that is a different claim about the game.

GF-18-MAP-01.why: the Map tab on a fresh-ish save: load, press the tab's shortcut, shoot. The cheapest frame outside the title screen.

GF-03-VILLAGE-02.why: street level between Tam, Oskar and Mira. A position the seeded save already reaches; the cost is the walk.

GF-14-COMBAT-02.why: CB-02, the practice trainer at (13,9). The trainer stands where the save left him, so the staging is the walk plus the fight -- but the FIGHT is the state, and a fight is never restored.

GF-19-UI-10.why: the first level-up announcement, which is an on-screen event a few frames wide. It follows from the trainer fight, so it is reproducible -- but only by fighting, and only if the restaged fight levels the same creature.

GF-20-NIGHT-01.why: 'first natural nightfall, no torch'. The precondition is the world clock reaching night through play, which S02-exit does not carry. Class D, and the reason S03C cannot be described as a short approach.

GF-20-NIGHT-02.why: the same position with the torch drawn: same clock, same staging, one extra press.

GF-14-COMBAT-13a.why: CB-13's night half -- a fight under torch light. Class D twice over: it needs the nightfall AND an encounter inside it.

steps.observation: Added 2026-09-02, FINDING-S03-105-HOME-MATERIALS-ROOT-CAUSE-2026-09-02.md. This is the FIRST gather node in the ladder, and unlike every later node it had no individual equip step of its own -- S03-56c..j binds axe/pickaxe/knife to hotbar slots 2/3/4 but never itself presses a hotbar button to make one ACTIVE, so this node was worked with nothing equipped and yielded no wood (0 of 7 wood attempts at this specific position, gate-f-run-20260902T122646Z-s03full). Every later node already has its own equip step for exactly this reason; this one was missing it by omission, not by design -- the ladder was authored assuming the last S03-56 assign (axe, S03-56i) would leave axe equipped, but assigning a tool to a hotbar slot and equipping it are two different actions.

steps.title: walk to the creature bed just built
steps.expected: one of the three creature beds built above is reachable nearby
steps.observation: Tightened again 2026-09-02 (second pass): the previous within:1.2, computed from ONE run's measured 4.0m camp-to-bed separation (< half of it, so the walk could never land closer to camp than to the bed by the triangle inequality), was not tight enough on a later run whose relative stick-placement (S03-121n/131n/141n) happened to land the pieces closer together: that run's own S03-205a reported 'walked 2.7 m ... in 35 walking frames' -- a short, nearly-direct walk, consistent with a SMALLER separation than 4.0m that time -- and S03-205b still read camp's own 'Rest until morning' instead of the bed's 'Rest a Creature'. The relative placement offsets (a fixed stick deflection for a fixed frame count, S03-121n/131n/141n) do not guarantee a fixed separation between pieces run to run, so a within tuned to one run's measured gap is not safe in general -- only a tighter margin buys more headroom against that variance. 0.6 halves the previous figure; if a future run's own placed_buildings measurement shows a separation under roughly 1.2 m (where 0.6 stops guaranteeing the triangle-inequality property), this needs ralph/OWNER-0902-REST-VISIBILITY's own fix (its name is literally this problem), not a third harness-side tightening -- a shared interact-prompt RADIUS two pieces of furniture can be placed inside of is not something a walk-stopping-distance can out-tune forever.

steps.title: put the active companion away, if one is standing in the way
steps.expected: the piloted creature follows the player everywhere, including up to a piece of furniture just built next to where it is standing -- its own 'Put <name> away' prompt is right on top of the player and can out-rank the bed's 'Rest a Creature' the same way camp's 'Rest until morning' can, for the identical reason (interaction_arbiter.gd's priority-then-nearest, and the companion is about as close as anything can be). optional:true because most of the time nothing is in the way at all -- this only presses when the live prompt actually says 'Put'.
steps.observation: Added 2026-09-02: measured directly across two consecutive runs, a different party member each time ('Put Mudsnout away' once -- a wild creature caught earlier that run -- then 'Put Bramblebun away', one of the scripted catch targets), both times blocking S03-205b in exactly the same shape the camp/bed within-tightening (FINDING-S03-205-CAMP-BED-PROMPT-COLLISION-2026-09-02.md and its follow-up) was written for, but with a THIRD contender no within value can out-tune: a deployed companion stands at ~0m from the player by definition, so no walk-stopping-distance can ever put the bed closer than it is. Putting it away first -- the same thing a real player would do before reaching past their own creature for a piece of furniture -- removes that contender before S03-205b ever presses.

This segment's own catch loop (S03-32a..38j, RIG-18) can faint the player's only creature on a real, non-buggy roll -- exactly what this run's own telemetry shows happened at t=256 ('Moss fainted', combat_hit, hp 0.0/1.18) -- and `encounter_director.gd::summon_active_creature()` (L864) refuses to deploy a fainted creature, so `can_challenge()` (L1568) then refuses EVERY trainer/gate fight for the rest of the game, with no error and no on-screen explanation (`trainer_npc.gd::_on_challenged` L171-172 falls back to the trainer's `defeated` conversation line whenever `can_challenge()` is false for ANY reason, not only an actual prior win). This is not a movement or collision defect: the South Bridge gate (`gated_crossing.gd`) is a real, correctly-locked physical barrier that only opens once its trainer is beaten, and a `move_to` step asked to walk through it can never succeed while the party's only creature stays fainted -- see `ralph/reports/handover-T2-STRANDING-2026-08-30.md`. `data/config/progression.json`'s own `creature_bed` comment: 'sleeping through the night completes any occupied bed immediately.' This step and the three after it assign the party's only creature to a bed here, before this segment's own S03-223..227 sleep step, so the sleep that was already going to happen actually revives it -- the same recovery a real player reaches by walking to the beds this segment just built for exactly this.

steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit. A walk that begins while a narrative modal still owns input does not fail as 'a modal is open' -- it fails as 'did not reach', many steps and sometimes many minutes later, which is how X04 lost its whole combat block to 3601 held frames. This assert is diagnostic and changes no behaviour: it turns that silent cascade into one named cause at the point of origin. RIG-25's rule, applied to narrative modals rather than to shop panels.
